headline_marked: Dhaka court cancels film actress Pori Moni’s bail, [[issues arrest warrant]]
headline: Dhaka court cancels film actress Pori Moni’s bail, issues arrest warrant
summary: Pori Moni's bail has been revoked by a Dhaka court in a 2022 case. An arrest warrant has been issued for the actress, who is expected to surrender tomorrow.
details: A Dhaka court has cancelled the bail of popular film actress Pori Moni and issued an arrest warrant in a case filed in 2022. The case was lodged by former Uttara Club Limited president Nasir U Mahmud over allegations including assault, vandalism, attempted murder, and intimidation.
The order was passed by Dhaka Senior Judicial Magistrate Mahfuzur Rahman. Pori Moni's lawyer stated that the actress is scheduled to surrender before the court tomorrow to seek fresh bail.

Court sources indicated that the case was up for witness testimony today. The prosecution requested the cancellation of Pori Moni's bail, while her defence sought an adjournment, citing her illness due to an allergy.

The court accepted the prosecution's plea, leading to the cancellation of her bail and the issuance of the arrest warrant. This development follows a charge sheet submitted on March 18, 2024, by Inspector Md Monir Hossain of the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI), Dhaka district, against Pori Moni and her costume designer, Junaid Karim Jimmy.

Charges against Pori Moni and Jimmy were accepted by the court on April 18, 2024. Another individual, Fatema-tuz-Jannat Bony, was discharged after the investigation found no evidence of her involvement. The court formally framed charges against Pori Moni and Jimmy on January 26, 2025.

This case is separate from a previous one filed by Pori Moni on June 14, 2021, with Savar Police Station. In that complaint, she accused Nasir and two others of attempting to rape and murder her during an incident on June 9 of the same year.
caption:

headline_marked: 100+ garment factories shut as [[workers protest for Tk 30,000 wage]]
headline: 100+ garment factories shut as workers protest for Tk 30,000 wage
summary: Clashes erupted in Savar and Ashulia as thousands of workers blocked roads, leading to police using tear gas and sound grenades to restore order.
details: Over 100 garment factories in Savar and Ashulia declared holidays today following widespread worker protests demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.
Between 30,000 and 40,000 workers gathered near Padmar Mor, blocking roads and clashing with police in several areas, including Ulail, Fulbaria, and Hemayetpur.
During the unrest, protesters set fire to a vehicle used by the officer-in-charge of Savar Model Police Station, who was seriously injured in the attack.
Police responded by firing tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse the crowds. One person was detained after detonating a crude bomb in the Hemayetpur area.
Four journalists were injured while covering the events, including Nazmul Huda, president of the Savar Press Club, who was assaulted during a live broadcast.

Police have arrested over 30 people, stating that third-party groups were exploiting workers' emotions to destabilize the country. Investigations are ongoing to check for links to banned organizations.
caption:
100+ factories shut and thousands of workers on the streets. Clashes erupt over wage demands.

Over 100 garment factories in Savar and Ashulia declared holidays today following widespread worker protests demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.

Between 30,000 and 40,000 workers gathered near Padmar Mor, blocking roads and clashing with police in several areas, including Ulail, Fulbaria, and Hemayetpur.

During the unrest, protesters set fire to a vehicle used by the officer-in-charge of Savar Model Police Station, who was seriously injured in the attack.

Police responded by firing tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse the crowds. One person was detained after detonating a crude bomb in the Hemayetpur area.

Four journalists were injured while covering the events, including Nazmul Huda, president of the Savar Press Club, who was assaulted during a live broadcast.

Police have arrested over 30 people, stating that third-party groups were exploiting workers' emotions to destabilize the country. Investigations are ongoing to check for links to banned organizations.
